owner: W1-17. RI-DLG03 §A/§C — 30 cell-filtered greetings per Tier A settlement, five disposition bands, >=4 per band, >=70% naming the town.
authored_order_rule: Within a class, entries are authored HIGHEST disposition minimum first. First-match-wins means the reverse order would make every warm greeting unreachable — the exact bug class RI-DLG01 step 4 lints for.

greetings.x: %PCName. This one saw you on the stair and came down. Friend, Lilmoth is yours today. Ask anything.
It is you, dry-one, and I have kept something back for you all week, a little secret about this town, and I would rather give it to you than to any purse in this town.

%PCName. Good. I have been holding a question about Lilmoth that I could not put to a colleague without it becoming a matter, and you are not a colleague, which today is a considerable recommendation.
%PCName. Off duty in an hour. Lilmoth is quiet. Ask me anything you like.

You are welcome at this door, %PCName, which is not a formula in Lilmoth and has not been said to an outsider by me in twenty years, and I would like you to understand that before you ask me whatever it is.
This one is Teel-Ma and this one works the roof-walks. Friend, Lilmoth is a hard town and you are asking politely. What is it?
Welcome to Lilmoth, which is a port, a ruin and an administrative fiction in roughly equal parts, and I will happily tell you about any of the three if you have the afternoon.
Customs, Lilmoth stair. Sergeant Verus. You're not carrying anything I care about. Ask.
You've given me something before and I remember it, dry-one. Lilmoth isn't a town where people remember things like that. So ask me, and I'll try to be worth it.
You have come to the door of a keeper in Lilmoth, which means you have walked past four people who would have told you not to, and I am obliged to say that says something for you.
This is Lilmoth. Stair is that way. Ask your question, citizen.
Lilmoth, yes. Everything sells here. Friend, what do you want?
You are in Lilmoth and you are looking for something, and in this town those are generally the same sentence. Name it and I will tell you which floor it is on.
You are new in Lilmoth and it shows in the way you are looking at the water, dry-one, and I will answer a question if you have one because the answering costs me nothing.
Lilmoth. Yes. And? Make it quick, stranger.
This one is busy. Lilmoth is busy. Say it.
Got a question about Lilmoth? Ask it. Got several? Don't.
You want something, and all of Lilmoth wants something, dry-one, and I have learned not to be hopeful about which sort you are going to turn out to be.
Move along. Lilmoth is full. Go and be somewhere else.
No. This one does not talk to you. Go.
Were I obliged to speak to everyone who came to Lilmoth, I would speak to no one. Good day.
I've nothing, and you've already taken the only thing I did have, dry-one, which was a quiet afternoon on a warm plank. So no. I won't be answering anything.
%PCTitle. In Lilmoth. Friend, this one will not forget the day.
%PCTitle. Stair's open. You won't be asked for a manifest today.
They're calling you %PCTitle on the boards now, dry-one, and I've been telling the whole town I knew you before the boards had your name. It is true. And not one of them believes me.
%PCTitle. I have had to open a new heading in the Lilmoth register for you, which the Office will query, and I intend to enjoy answering the query enormously.
So it's finished, %PCTitle. Lilmoth's still standing, and the water's still coming in at the rate it always did. And I find I'm glad about the second thing, in a way I didn't expect.
%PCTitle. Cart is open. Friend, your money is no good on this stair.
Second stair, low water. Friend, this one sells there and not here.
The house advances against a cargo and takes the manifest as security, and I would advise you to read what the manifest says about the cargo before you sign anything about the cargo.
%PCName. Good to see you on the wall street. Stormhold owes you one. Ask.
%PCName, and welcome. Stormhold isn't an interesting town, and I've been happier here since you started asking me questions that are. So please. Go on.
%PCName. Weigh house cheats. Friend, that is free, and Stormhold would fine this one for saying it.
You are the only person in Stormhold who says my name, dry-one, and I would tell you anything at all that I happened to know, and I happen to know a good deal.
There is no well in Stormhold and so there is nothing here I can give you, %PCName, except what I know, and today you may have all of it.
Ninth Cohort, Stormhold garrison. You are welcome at the gate. What do you need, citizen?
Welcome to Stormhold, the only town in Argonia with working drains, of which we are proud in a manner that visitors find difficult to take seriously and which is entirely justified.
This one is Jeel and this one has a cart. Friend, welcome to Stormhold. What are you buying?
You've been decent to me twice in this town, dry-one, and Stormhold isn't generous. So ask what you like, and I won't stretch it.
Since you are here and since Stormhold is tedious, provincial, you may as well ask me something. I am told I answer well when bored.
Stormhold. Wall, gate, market, muster. Which one, citizen?
Stormhold. Everything has a fee. Friend, what is your business?
You're in Stormhold, which is a garrison with a market attached. There's very little in it I can't point you at in one sentence. Try me.
Stormhold is dry underfoot and hard on the sleeping, dry-one, and if that is the sort of thing you wanted to know then I am your man for the rest of it too.
This is Stormhold. State it, stranger.
Stormhold. Fees. Guards. Say it fast.
If it concerns Stormhold, be brief. If it concerns me, be briefer.
People in Stormhold talk to me when they want directions and never otherwise, dry-one, so I suppose you want directions.
No. Move on! Stormhold's not for you.
Cart is closed. Go.
Unless you have brought an instrument bearing a seal, provincial, you are wasting a morning that was already poor.
You walked past me four times in Stormhold before you wanted something, dry-one, and now you want something, and I find I have nothing for you.
%PCTitle. Gate's open. Fee's waived. And don't argue about it.
%PCTitle. Stormhold has put your name in the muster book without a rank beside it, which is unprecedented and which the tribune has declined to explain.
%PCTitle, in Stormhold. Friend, this one will charge you nothing and tell everyone.
%PCTitle now, is it, dry-one, and you still stopped, and that is worth more to me than the title is to you.
There was never a well in Stormhold, %PCTitle, and there's one now. Three feet down, under the north drain. And there isn't a soul who knows what to do about it.
Should the province remember any of this in ninety years, %PCTitle, it will remember it wrongly. Presumably that is acceptable to you.
Chit or nothing. Quartermaster's on the wall street. Don't try the store.
Weigh house takes all comers. Friend, and takes a little off all of them.
You are known at this root now, %PCName, and Helstrom does not do that quickly or often, and the fact that it has done it for an outsider is going to be discussed for a generation.
%PCName. You have been inside the halls, which no surveyor has managed in a hundred and forty years, and I would trade a great deal for one afternoon of your recollections of Helstrom.
%PCName. Past the second root. Friend, this one has never been. Tell this one everything.
They let you into Helstrom proper, dry-one, and they haven't let me past the carriers' shed in nine years. I'm not bitter about it. And I'm a little bitter about it.
%PCName. Twenty of us outside the third root. You go in. We don't. Ask me anything.
Welcome to Helstrom, which is not a welcome anyone here gives lightly, and it means only that you may walk to the second root and no further until those who are owed a say have had one.
Helstrom. And you've already noticed it doesn't have streets, which puts you ahead of the last three Imperial visitors. All of whom asked me for a map.
This one is Wades-Deep and this one carries. Friend, welcome to Helstrom. Nothing rolls here.
Cohort outpost, Helstrom. We stay outside. You may not have to. Ask.
There is food at the carriers' shed for any back in Helstrom that will lift, dry-one, and I lift badly and they feed me anyway, and that is the town in one sentence.
This is Helstrom and you are under the second root, supplicant, and if you tell me what you are looking for I will tell you which root it is under.
Helstrom. No carts. All carried. Friend, what do you need moved?
Helstrom. Outpost's behind you. Inside isn't ours. Question, citizen?
You are standing in Helstrom, which is grown rather than built, and every direction I can give you will be in terms of roots rather than distances. Say the name and we will manage.
Helstrom is not a place a stranger asks questions in, and you are asking, so ask the one that matters and not the other four.
Helstrom. Outpost only. Nothing for you here, stranger.
This one carries. This one does not guide. Ask someone else.
You are the fourth outsider in Helstrom this season and the other three wanted directions too, dry-one, and none of them gave me anything for them.
You are not placed here and you have not been brought, and until one of those changes there is nothing that may be said to you in Helstrom, and I am sorry, and it is not going to change today.
Back to the outpost line. Now! Helstrom's not a town you wander in.
No. Not to you. Not in Helstrom.
Even I have somewhere to be in Helstrom, dry-one, which tells you how little I want to stand here having this conversation with you.
%PCTitle. The name has gone down the roots ahead of you, which is not a figure of speech in Helstrom, and there are keepers at the fourth hall who have been waiting since the spring.
%PCTitle. In Helstrom. Friend, this one carried your bags once.
%PCTitle. We stood outside and you went in. The outpost has stopped pretending otherwise.
%PCTitle. I have begun a Helstrom file, which is the first one the annexe has held since the third abandoned survey, and I am aware that starting it may be the most consequential thing I ever do.
The third root is thickening, %PCTitle, and it has not thickened in six years, and I do not have a word for what I feel about that and neither does anyone else at this well.
They've given me a hall, dry-one. A real one. And I didn't ask, and I don't know who decided, and I haven't slept in it yet, because I keep expecting a clerk to come and correct the mistake.
By the root, not the mile. Friend, that is the rate and it does not move.
What is given at a well is not sold and is not refused, and a supplicant who arrives hurt is tended before they are asked a single question about who they are.
